verses.english: A Question About the Dimension of Neither Perception Nor Non-Perception
“They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of neither perception nor non-perception’.
What is the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception?

verses.pali: ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.
This is called the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

verses.pali: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
verses.english: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.
verses.english: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of nothingness beset me.

verses.pali: Atha kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

verses.pali: Mā, brāhmaṇa, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ pamādo, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ saṇṭhapehi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ ekodiṁ karohi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ samādahā’ti.
verses.english: Don’t neglect the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

verses.pali: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja vihāsiṁ.
verses.english: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

verses.pali: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya …pe… mahābhiññataṁ patto”ti.
verses.english: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
